analysis:
The PR is documentation-only (docs/developer/build.md, docs/developer/test.md): date bumps plus CI runner routing text. No source, protocol, key-handling or attestation code changed, so TB-002 and TB-011 controls are untouched.

The documented change is that the macOS provider and cluster test jobs in ci.yml (test-provider shards, test-provider-sdk, test-cluster*, etc.) may now be routed to Darkbloom Sandbox runners (build.md lines 256-279, 262). Previously those macOS jobs were documented as pinned to literal Blacksmith labels. The change is described as read-only CI with a Blacksmith fallback. Per build.md lines 267-309, routing is off unless DARKBLOOM_ROUTING=on, fork PRs keep the fallback, and the route job has no token permissions or checkout. A grant is used only when it repeats the exact labels. Errors and malformed replies fall back. Release, signing, publication, model registration, review automation and cache warming on master stay on literal Blacksmith labels (build.md line 300). test.md line 1807 states that release workflows remain on literal labels.

One residual uncertainty is outside the supplied evidence: the actual workflow YAML (.github/workflows/ci.yml, darkbloom-route.yml) was not supplied. I cannot verify that routed macOS test jobs hold no secrets, that cache saves are limited to admitted branches, or that sandbox-runner isolation and trust (TB-013 and ADV-001 style supply-chain concerns) match the documentation. The docs say push runs on admitted branches save caches on Darkbloom, which is a cache-poisoning surface only if non-admitted code can write caches. build.md line 314 limits saves to master and dev pushes. These are workflow-level matters to verify, and the docs do not themselves create a regression. No finding is raised because it is documentation of an unverified implementation. A later pass on the workflow files should confirm the documented permission and secret boundaries.
